name: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
analogy: Think of it as a row of small magnifying glasses sliding along a chart, each tuned to spot one little shape such as a three-bar stall or a sharp wick. Later layers look at where the first glasses lit up and spot bigger shapes built from them, and a final judge turns the bigger shapes into a call.

steps.title: Lay the recent bars out as a grid
steps.description: The window is arranged as a grid, with bars along one side and the measurements (open, high, low, close, volume, indicators) along the other. A chart image works too, and then the grid is made of pixels.
steps.inExample: The last 60 five-minute MNQ bars are arranged as a table of 60 bars by 8 measurements.

steps.title: Slide small filters along the grid
steps.description: Each filter is a tiny window covering only a few bars at a time. It slides along the series, scoring how strongly each position matches the shape it has learned to find. The same filter is reused at every position, so a shape is found wherever it occurs.
steps.inExample: One filter, 3 bars wide, lights up wherever three bars stall near a low after a drop; it lights up at bars 21 and 47.

steps.title: Keep only the strongest responses
steps.description: A pooling step shrinks the output by keeping the strongest response in each small neighbourhood, so the model keeps the fact that a shape was present and drops its exact position. This makes it less sensitive to small shifts.
steps.inExample: The 60 filter scores per filter are cut to 30 by keeping the stronger of each pair of neighbouring positions.

steps.title: Stack more layers for bigger shapes
steps.description: The next layer applies filters to the output of the first, so it can find shapes made of smaller shapes, such as a drop, a stall and a bounce. Each layer sees a wider stretch of the series than the one before.
steps.inExample: A second layer lights up on the sequence of a drop, a stall and then a bounce spanning about 10 bars.

steps.title: Combine the shapes into a verdict
steps.description: The final feature values are flattened and fed to a small classifying layer that turns them into class probabilities. Training compares these probabilities with what really happened and adjusts all the filters to reduce the error.
steps.inExample: The classifier outputs: up 46 percent, flat 22 percent, down 32 percent for the next 6 bars.

useFor.task: Spotting local shapes in a window of bars
useFor.example: Detecting stalls, wicks and reversals within the last 60 five-minute MNQ bars as inputs to a direction call.
Labelling a picture of the last hour of one-minute candles as a hammer, engulfing bar or neither, as in the dashboard's candle vision study.
Running a one-dimensional CNN on streaming bars where speed matters more than long memory.
Letting a CNN compress the last 120 bars into 32 numbers that a gradient boosted tree then uses alongside indicators.

avoidWhen: The pattern depends on events far apart in the window, such as a reaction to something 200 bars ago; filters only see nearby bars, and attention or recurrent models reach further.
Your inputs are a table of unrelated indicators with no order; there is no neighbourhood for a filter to slide over, so a tree model is more natural.
You do not have enough data to train many filters; with a few months of bars a CNN will happily learn noise as shape.

example.scenario: At 14:35 Eastern a 5-minute MNQ bar closes. A CNN reads the last 60 bars and classifies the next 6 bars as up, flat or down, where flat means a move smaller than half the average true range.

input.summary: A grid of 60 bars by 8 measurements, scaled so levels do not dominate.

fields.name: window length
fields.meaning: How many five-minute bars the network looks at, five hours of trading.

fields.name: measurements per bar
fields.meaning: Open, high, low, close and volume as changes from the prior bar, plus three indicators.

fields.name: latest close
fields.meaning: The close of the newest bar.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent bar; flat is a move under 11 points.

fields.name: relative strength index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A momentum reading from 0 to 100; below 40 shows recent weakness.

output.summary: A probability for each of three classes and the shape that drove it.

fields.name: probability the move is up
fields.meaning: The chance the close 6 bars later is more than 11 points above this close.

fields.name: probability the move is flat
fields.meaning: The chance it ends within 11 points of this close.

fields.name: probability the move is down
fields.meaning: The chance it ends more than 11 points below this close.

fields.name: strongest shape
fields.meaning: The second-layer filter that responded most, over the last 10 bars.

example.reading: Up beats down by 14 points of probability, a mild lean that is dwarfed by costs unless the average win is large. Compare it with always guessing the most common class on held-out folds, since a CNN that does no better than the base rate has found nothing.
